Misuse and overuse of antimicrobials could undermine decades of medical progress and make even common infections increasingly difficult to treat, a senior health ministry official said on Wednesday, calling for collective action to contain antimicrobial resistance (AMR).
Addressing the national observance of World Antimicrobial Resistance Awareness Week 2026 virtually, Union Health Secretary Punya Salila Srivastava described AMR as one of the most serious public health challenges and stressed the need for a coordinated "One Health" approach to tackle it.
This year's theme is "One Health, One Action: Prevent AMR Now".
She said medicines that have saved countless lives are gradually losing their effectiveness due to misuse and overuse.
Srivastava highlighted the interconnectedness of human and animal health, plant and food systems and the environment, noting that improper use of antimicrobials across these sectors contributes to the emergence and spread of resistance.
She said the government has accorded high priority to containing AMR, with the National Action Plan on Antimicrobial Resistance 2.0 (NAP AMR 2.0), 2025-2029, providing a framework for surveillance, infection prevention, responsible antimicrobial use, research and coordinated action.
The health ministry's National Programme on AMR Containment, coordinated by the National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC), focuses on strengthening laboratory capacity for AMR surveillance, infection prevention and control, antimicrobial stewardship and awareness generation, she said.
Srivastava urged healthcare professionals to prescribe antibiotics only when clinically indicated and in accordance with treatment guidelines. She also asked pharmacists to ensure appropriate dispensing against valid prescriptions and counsel patients on their correct use.
She also advised people against self-medication, sharing antibiotics or using leftover medicines, stressing that antibiotics are not effective against viral infections such as the common cold and influenza.
More than half of antimicrobial sales in India take place without prescriptions, while nearly half of outpatient antibiotic prescriptions are inappropriate, participants at the event noted.
They called for scaling up public awareness campaigns, preventing self-prescription, ensuring proper disposal of antibiotics and expired medicines, and displaying legal warnings at drug shops against the sale of antimicrobials without prescriptions.
Participants also stressed the need to curb production of substandard and spurious medicines, promote appropriate antibiotic use in veterinary medicine, particularly for food-producing animals, and maintain quality standards in healthcare facilities to prevent infections.
The event was attended by senior officials from the National Health Systems Resource Centre, Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation, Department of Animal Husbandry, Indian Medical Association and All India Association of Druggists and Chemists, besides officials from states and Union territories.
World AMR Awareness Week is observed from November 18 to 24 every year to improve awareness and understanding of antimicrobial resistance and promote best practices among the public, policymakers and One Health stakeholders.

Vote for the first BBC Men's Footballer of the Year
- Published
Voting is now open for the BBC Men's Footballer of the Year 2026 award, which will be presented at Sports Personality of the Year.
Fans from the UK can vote from the five-player shortlist of Jude Bellingham, Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe, Rodri and Lamine Yamal.
The vote closes on Friday, 27 November at 09:00 GMT.
The winner of the award - new for this year - will be presented during the live Sports Personality of the Year show on Sunday, 13 December.
Alex Kay-Jelski, Director of BBC Sport, said: "From the drama and excitement of the men's World Cup to the moments that have captivated fans across the domestic and international game, 2026 has given us so much to celebrate.
"Our inaugural BBC Men's Footballer of the Year award is about recognising the players who have made this year so special, inspired fans and left their mark on the game.
"It's a fantastic shortlist, and I can't wait to see who the public choose as our first-ever winner."
The shortlist was selected by an expert panel comprising former international players and some of the BBC's most respected football voices, bringing together a wealth of experience and insight from across the game.
The panel included Cesar Azpilicueta (Spain), Scott Brown (Scotland), Olivier Giroud (France), Shay Given (Republic of Ireland), Hassan Kachloul (Morocco), Lucas Leiva (Brazil), Benni McCarthy (South Africa), Alan Shearer, Ellen White (both England) and Ashley Williams (Wales).
Read more on the five contenders and cast your vote below.
Jude Bellingham
Age: 23 Country: England
Club: Real Madrid Position: Midfield
Bellingham made history this summer as he became the first Englishman to score as many as seven goals at a major tournament.
In a superb World Cup for the midfielder, he memorably netted twice in back-to-back games to help the Three Lions beat Mexico and Norway.
That meant he joined exalted company as the first player to score two or more goals in successive World Cup knockout games since Diego Maradona in 1986, and the second youngest in history behind Pele in 1958.
Bellingham also became the youngest European player to make an appearance at four different major tournaments, and also reached the milestone of 50 caps at a younger age than any other England men's player.
The goals continued to flow for Real Madrid, too, with Bellingham notching his 50th for the club to move above the legendary Zinedine Zidane in the Los Blancos' all-time scoring charts.
Harry Kane
Age: 33 Country: England
Club: Bayern Munich Position: Forward
In a stunning year of goalscoring, Kane become the first Englishman for 25 years (and only fifth in history) to win the Ballon d'Or - awarded to the world's best footballer.
His tally of 73 goals in 65 matches for club and country during a stellar 2025-26 season has only been surpassed in one of Europe's top five leagues by Lionel Messi's 82 for Barcelona and Argentina in 2011-12.
Kane scored 61 of those goals in just 51 appearances for Bayern Munich as he helped the Bavarians to a league and cup double. His total was 19 more than any other player in Europe's top five divisions.
Already England's record goalscorer, he surpassed Peter Shilton's mark of 125 appearances to become the most-capped Englishman in history.
Six goals at this summer's World Cup also helped him overtake Gary Lineker as the Three Lions' record scorer at the tournament, while he joined David Beckham as the only Englishmen to score in three separate World Cups.
Kylian Mbappe
Age: 27 Country: France
Club: Real Madrid Position: Forward
Mbappe came out on top of an enthralling tussle with Lionel Messi at the 2026 World Cup to become the leading goalscorer in the tournament's history.
The France forward, who is still only 27, took his tally to 22 from just three World Cups to finish one ahead of the great Argentine.
Mbappe's 10 goals from eight games this summer meant he won his second World Cup Golden Boot - a feat no player has managed before.
It also made him the first man to reach double figures at a World Cup since Gerd Muller in 1970, with only Just Fontaine (13) and Sandor Kocsis (11) having scored more goals in a single tournament.
Other achievements in a standout year included him finishing runner-up in the Ballon d'Or awards and overtaking Olivier Giroud as France's all-time leading goalscorer.
He scored 25 times to retain his title as La Liga's top scorer during a 2025-26 campaign in which he netted 42 goals in all competitions for Real Madrid.
Rodri
Age: 30 Country: Spain
Club: Barcelona Position: Midfield
Midfield maestro Rodri earned yet another accolade in his incredible career when he was awarded the Golden Ball trophy for the World Cup's best player.
By captaining Spain to glory in the US, Rodri became only the fourth male player to win the World Cup, European Championship, Champions League and Ballon d'Or - following in the footsteps of legendary Germans Gerd Muller and Franz Beckenbauer and France's Zinedine Zidane.
His achievements were made all the more special given doubts remained over whether he would recapture his best form after a long recovery from a serious knee injury in 2024.
Then Manchester City boss Pep Guardiola predicted he would return to his best at the World Cup and he was right. Rodri completed 756 passes there - the most in the tournament since records began in 1966.
His final season at Manchester City before departing for Barcelona ended in familiar fashion with a domestic cup double taking his trophy haul with the club to 14.
Lamine Yamal
Age: 19 Country: Spain
Club: Barcelona Position: Forward
Lamine Yamal continues to rewrite the record books with his astonishing exploits for club and country.
Just days after his 19th birthday, the Spaniard became the youngest footballer to have played in - and won - both a World Cup and a European Championship. The only players younger than him to play in a World Cup final are Brazil's Pele in 1958 and Giuseppe Bergomi for Italy in 1982.
For the second year running, his performances led to a podium place at the Ballon d'Or and at the same award ceremony he became the first footballer in history to win the Young Talent of the Year three years in succession.
At club level, he was named La Liga's Best Player courtesy of a starring role in Barcelona's title success. The teenager ended the season with an impressive 24 goals and 18 assists across all competitions.
He recently broke Kylian Mbappe's record for the most goals by a teenager in Champions League history.

You can upscale low-resolution photos for free using offline AI tools. Use Upscayl on Mac and Windows, Upscal on iPhone, or Offline AI Image Upscaler on Android. These apps enhance image resolution up to 4x without uploading your photos to the cloud, keeping them private.
If there is one area where AI has truly revolutionized, apart from writing and coding, it is image upscaling. Whether it’s your old photo taken on a Sony Cyber-shot or one that’s completely distorted, you can give it to AI and you can get a clean, high-resolution version without changing its original form.
Not just your old photos, you can also upscale any standard photo taken on modern phones to the highest resolution possible.
However, one downside of using AI to upscale images, especially if you care about privacy, is that your images need to be uploaded to the cloud for any AI provider, processed there, and then sent back to your smartphone.
Although those images won’t be public, some companies use them to train their AI models. This is the reason why many users, even we, think twice before uploading sensitive photos to AI models for upscaling
Fortunately, tools like Upscayl let the AI model run locally on your device and upscale images to the highest possible resolution without your data leaving your device. Although it has specific hardware requirements, most modern PCs and smartphones support it, and it’s faster too.
It also supports batch processing, where you can upscale multiple images at once. The quality is pretty good too. In this guide, I will show you how to set up Upscayl, a local image upscaler on your Mac, Windows, Android, and iPhone.
Table of Contents
How to Upscale Low-Resolution Photos Locally for Free
Please note that the original Upscayl is only available on desktop platforms like Windows, Mac, and Linux; there are also free apps that use similar technology and work well. I will cover everything in this guide together and help you set up a free image upscaler locally on your device. This guide is designed for beginners, so every step is comprehensive and detailed.
You don’t need much setup to upscale images locally. Since everything comes in one package, the process is very straightforward. You can download the upscaler app; it installs the upscaler model locally and includes a beginner-friendly interface, making it even easier for first-time users.
Below are the steps for each device.
How to upscale photos on a Mac with Upscayl
Step 1: Open Safari or any browser, visit upscayl.org in the address bar, and press Return. On the page, click on the Download button at the top right
Step 2: Now, on the download page, you can see download options for various platforms, including macOS. However, do not click on the macOS button. It opens the Mac App Store, where Upscayl is a paid app. The same app is available for free from Upscayl’s own website.
Step 3: Tap on the alternative download option below and select the DMG version of the app
Step 4: Once downloaded, install the app on your Mac
Step 5: Open the app and complete the onboarding steps. They’re straightforward and easy to follow.
Step 6: Now using Upscayl is easy. In the sidebar, under Step 1, tap Select Image, or drag and drop the image into the right pane.
Step 7: Next, once the image is uploaded, under Step 2, choose an AI model. Upscayl Standard is the best choice for most images. You can also select a different model based on your preference.
Step 8: Now set Image Scale to 4x. This setting makes the image width and height four times larger, so a 480 by 320 photo becomes 1920 by 1280 pixels. You can also drag the slider to change it.
Step 9: Next, under Step 3, you can set where Upscayl saves the new upscaled image. To save it in a preferred location, click Set output folder and choose a folder.
Step 10: Finally, under Step 4, click Upscayl. Depending on your settings and your hardware, it can take a couple of seconds to a minute to upscale images.
Step 11: Once it is done, you can compare the changes. Drag the slider in the middle of the picture to compare the original (left) with the upscaled version (right). The upscaled image will be saved in the folder you set in step 9, or next to your original image file on your Mac.
How to upscale photos on Windows with Upscayl
Next, let’s see how you can upscale images on Windows using Upscayl. The process is very similar to the Mac.
Step 1: Open Microsoft Edge or any browser, go to upscayl.org, and click Download in the top-right corner of the header.
Step 2: Now, on the download page, click the Windows button to start downloading (about 250 MB)
Step 3: Once downloaded, click the file to open it and go through the setup process. If Windows prompts you to allow this app from an unknown publisher, click Yes to start installing.
Step 4: Now select the installation folder; I recommend you keep the suggested installation folder and click Install.
Step 5: Finally, once installed, click Finish to complete the installation on your Windows.
Step 6: Now open the app and go through the setup process. It is very straightforward and easy to follow.
Step 7: Using Upscayl is easy; in Step 1, select an image. If you want to upscale multiple images, turn on the toggle that says ” Batch upscale above Step 1
Step 8: Select the image you want to upscale and tap on Open
Step 9: Now select the upscale model. The Upscayl Standard is best for most photos. Tap it and change it based on your preference. You can also increase the image scale to 4x. By default, it is 4x.
Step 10: Now, in step three, select the desired folder where you want to store the upscaled images, or keep the default, which stores the upscaled version right next to the original file, and tap the Upscayl button to upscale your images
How to upscale photos on iPhone with Upscayl
Upscayl.org is not available for mobile phones. However, free apps let you upscale images locally on your device. Some apps also offer an optional paid plan, but most features are free. Here are the two best upscaling apps.
Step 1: Download the Upscal Enhance Video and Image app on iPhone. Use this link.
Step 2: Once the app is installed, open the app and switch over to the image option
Step 3: Now you can select images from Photos or Files. In this case, I’m choosing the image from my files.
Step 4: The app shows your photo’s current resolution and how much you can upgrade it. In my case, my 480 by 320 photo can be upscaled to 1920 by 1280. Next, tap the settings bar just above Start upscaling. It shows the current model, scale, and format. You can tap the settings icon to customize the model, Upscaling methods, and more.
Step 5: Once you’ve made your changes, tap the Start Upscaling button and wait for the image to upscale. Once complete, you will see the completed status; tap Save to Photos to save the upscaled images to your Photos app.
How to upscale photos on Android with Offline AI Image Upscaler
Similar to iPhone, you can download the Offline AI Upscaler app by Bytesweavers to upscale photos locally on your Android
Step 1: Open the Play Store and download the Offline AI Image Upscaler app by Bytesweavers on your Android phone. You can use this link.
Step 2: Now open the app and tap on Choose photo, then select the image you want to upscale
Step 3: The app shows your photo and the resolution it will make. In my case, it’s 1920 by 1280. To edit the model, you can find the model settings below the photo. The default model is set to Photo AI, which is recommended. However, you can also choose a different model based on your needs.
Step 4: Once you’ve customized it, click Enhance Photo, and that’s it. The app will enhance your photo for a few minutes and when it’s done, drag the slider on the photo to compare the original with the enhanced version. Once you’re done, you can save the photo in different formats.
Give Your Old Photos a New Life With AI
This is how to set up an offline image AI upscaler on Windows, Mac, Android, and iPhone. This setup works completely offline, and many of these methods also support batch processing to upscale your images.
However, for local AI image models, Upscayl is currently the best option. However, it is not as good as any online model. Although it reduces pixelation, it adds softness; if the original image is too distorted and has fewer details, it can soften the image. In most cases with decent images, though, the upscaled version works well. But again, it all depends upon the quality of the original image.
Also remember that upscaling an image multiple times doesn’t improve its quality. Only the first output is the highest quality you can get. I hope you find this detailed and comprehensive guide helpful. If you have any issues setting up the local AI image upscaler on your device, let me know in the comments, and I will be happy to help.

Why a shortage of clinical psychologists in Keralam govt hospitals is leaving people with intellectual disabilities waiting for certificates
As per the last Kerala Disability Census in 2015, there are about 80,000 persons with various intellectual challenges. However, government hospitals and medical college hospitals in the State currently have only 22 clinical psychologists to conduct IQ assessment tests
Updated - November 21, 2026 01:40 pm IST - Kozhikode
As per the latest disability assessment guidelines issued by the Union government’s Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, differently-abled children must undergo assessment tests at least thrice before they turn 18 to obtain permanent disability certificates. (file image)
| Photo Credit: K. Ragesh
People with intellectual disabilities in Keralam are struggling to obtain and renew disability certificates due to a severe shortage of clinical psychologists in government hospitals to conduct Intelligence Quotient (IQ) assessment tests.
As per the latest disability assessment guidelines issued by the Union government’s Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, differently-abled children must undergo assessment tests at least thrice before they turn 18 to obtain permanent disability certificates. During all these assessment phases, an IQ test is a must. However, there are only 22 clinical psychologists under the Directorate of Health Services (DHS) and the Directorate of Medical Education (DME) put together – 17 under the DHS and the rest under the DME.

Last week, international health authorities formally announced that the US had lost its measles-elimination status, meaning that the virus is once again endemic. But the official determination is a bit like getting the technical readout of a cracked dam while the country is already feet under water.
The national tally of measles cases is nearing 6,000 for the year, the highest count since 1991. Transmission is widespread, with 47 states and jurisdictions reporting cases. There have been 43 outbreaks this year, which account for 96 percent of the cases. Four states have case counts above 500, including Pennsylvania, which leads with 1,638 cases as of November 23. Nearly 650 people have been hospitalized nationwide. As of today, 14 people have died.
Deaths and transmission
On November 23, Pennsylvania’s health department announced its ninth confirmed death, an unvaccinated resident of Centre County. On November 24, Wisconsin reported its third measles death, an adult in Lafayette County. The report follows two other deaths in the state, an infant and a child. New York has also reported a death, which was of a 7-month-old baby. On November 20, Virginia reported the death of a child between the age of 0 and 4.
The virus isn’t slowing down. Measles is the most contagious virus known; it can linger in the air for up to two hours. Up to 90 percent of people who are not immune will fall ill after an exposure. People are considered immune if they’ve been vaccinated or previously infected. With slipping vaccination rates nationwide, the number of susceptible people is only growing.
To keep measles from getting a foothold in a community, vaccination rates need to be 95 percent or higher. According to the latest data, only 92.4 percent of US kindergartners were vaccinated with the measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine in the 2025–2026 school year. Only 10 states have MMR vaccination rates at or above the 95 percent threshold. But even in those states, there are pockets and communities that are undervaccinated.

20 నవంబర్ 2026న ముంబైలోని కుర్లా వెస్ట్‌లో, ఫీనిక్స్ మార్కెట్‌సిటీ మాల్ సమీపంలోని ప్రమోద్ మహాజన్ గార్డెన్‌లో ఒక యువ జంటపై కొంతమంది మైనర్లు దాడి చేశారు. ఒక గుంపు ఆ జంటను చుట్టుముట్టి, అసభ్యంగా ప్రవర్తిస్తూ,  దాడి చేసారు. ఈ దాడికి సంబంధించిన వీడియో వైరల్ కావడంతో పోలీసులు ఎనిమిది మంది మైనర్లపై కేసు నమోదు చేశారు. వారిని 4 డిసెంబర్ 2026 వరకు జువైనల్ కరెక్షనల్ హోమ్‌కు పంపించారు (ఇక్కడ, ఇక్కడ).
ఈ ఘటన నేపథ్యంలో, పోలీసులు కొంతమంది వ్యక్తులను ఊరేగిస్తున్నట్లు చూపించే వీడియో ఒకటి సోషల్ మీడియాలో (ఇక్కడ, ఇక్కడ, ఇక్కడ) వైరల్ అవుతోంది. ముంబైలో యువ జంటపై దాడి చేసిన వారిని పోలీసులు ఇలా ఊరేగిస్తున్నారని ఈ వీడియోను షేర్ చేస్తున్నారు. ఈ పోస్టులో చేసిన వాదనలో నిజమెంత ఉందో ఇప్పుడు పరిశీలిద్దాం.
క్లెయిమ్: ముంబైలోని కుర్లా వెస్ట్‌లో యువ జంటపై దాడి చేసిన నిందితులను ముంబై పోలీసులు రోడ్డు పై ఊరేగిస్తున్నట్లు ఈ వీడియో చూపిస్తోంది.
ఫాక్ట్: ఈ వైరల్ వీడియోలో గుజరాత్‌లోని సూరత్‌లో 18 ఏళ్ల సంతోష్ మోరే హత్య కేసులో అరెస్టైన నిందితులను చూపిస్తున్నారు. ఈ హత్య కేసుకు సంబంధించి సూరత్ పోలీసులు నిందితులను ఊరేగించారు. ముంబైలో యువ జంటపై దాడి చేసిన వారిని కాదు. కాబట్టి, ఈ పోస్టులో చేసిన వాదన తప్పు.
వైరల్ వీడియోలోని కీ ఫ్రేమ్‌లతో రివర్స్ ఇమేజ్ సెర్చ్ చేయగా, 2026 నవంబర్ 14న Gujarat Live అనే ఇన్‌స్టాగ్రామ్ ఖాతాలో అప్‌లోడ్ చేసిన వీడియో లభించింది. ఈ వీడియో ముంబైలోని కుర్లా ఘటనకు ముందే అప్‌లోడ్ చేయబడింది. ఆ వీడియోలో ఉన్న వివరణలో, సూరత్‌కు చెందిన యువకుడు సంతోష్ మోరే హత్య కేసులో అరెస్టైన నిందితులను చూపిస్తున్నట్లు పేర్కొన్నారు.
దీనిపై కీవర్డ్ సెర్చ్ చేయగా, వైరల్ వీడియోలోని దృశ్యాలతో కూడిన పలు మీడియా రిపోర్టులు (ఇక్కడ, ఇక్కడ) లభించాయి. ఈ రిపోర్టుల ప్రకారం, 8 నవంబర్ 2026న సూరత్‌లోని రసూలాబాద్ ప్రాంతంలో 18 ఏళ్ల సంతోష్ మోరేను కత్తితో పొడిచి హత్య చేసినట్లు ఆరోపణలు ఉన్నాయి. ప్రేమ వ్యవహారానికి సంబంధించిన వివాదం, గత కక్షల కారణంగా ఈ హత్య జరిగినట్లు సమాచారం. ఈ కేసులో జావేద్ అలియాస్ నవాబ్ షేక్, హన్సరాజ్ కుష్వాహా, షకీబ్ మానియార్, షాహిద్ షేక్, పీయూష్ సాహూలను నిందితులుగా గుర్తించారు.
2026 నవంబర్ 12న సూరత్ పోలీసులు తమ X ఖాతాలో అప్‌లోడ్ చేసిన వీడియోలో కూడా ఇలాంటి దృశ్యాలే కనిపించాయి. ఈ వీడియోలో అదే నిందితులను పోలీసులు ఊరేగించడం చూడవచ్చు. ఈ వీడియోకు జత చేసిన వివరణలో, ఖటోదరా పోలీస్ స్టేషన్ పరిధిలోని ఆజాద్ నగర్‌లో ఒక యువకుడి హత్య కేసులో నిందితులను ఖటోదరా పోలీసులు అరెస్టు చేసి, చట్టం గురించి వారికి గుణపాఠం చెప్పారని పేర్కొన్నారు.
చివరిగా, హత్య కేసులో నిందితులను సూరత్ పోలీసులు ఊరేగిస్తున్న వీడియోను, ముంబైలో యువ జంటపై దాడి చేసిన ఘటనకు సంబంధించినదిగా షేర్ చేస్తున్నారు.

Suresh Mittal is 87. According to Uttar Pradesh’s latest draft electoral roll, his father, Vansh Mittal, is 23. Both are registered at house number 869 in booth 111 of the Dholana constituency in Hapur. The same roll lists Vansh as the son of Ajay, a 56-year-old in the same house.
Suresh is not an exception. Alt News found 1,10,875 voters in the Special Summary Revision (SSR) draft roll whose father or mother, registered in the same booth and the same house, is recorded as the same age as them or younger. The draft was published on November 17.
A Year of Revisions: First SIR, Now SSR
The draft comes at the end of a long year for UP’s voter list. The Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the rolls began on October 27, 2025 and ended with the final roll on April 10, 2026. In those 166 days the state’s electorate shrank from 15.44 crore to 13.39 crore.
As per the process of SIR, every voter was supposed to be issued an enumeration form, which was supposed to be collected by booth-level officers (BLOs). The Election Commission’s software then allegedly went through the data looking for what it called logical discrepancies. One of these was a parent less than 15 years older than the voter. About 2.22 crore voters in UP were sent notices for such discrepancies, and the Commission says hearings were completed on all of them.
On October 15, six months after the SIR’s final roll, the Election Commission ordered a Special Summary Revision (SSR) in 17 states and Union territories, including UP. The SSR draft roll, which merges the SIR roll with all supplementary lists, has 13.58 crore electors. Claims and objections can be filed till December 16, and the final roll is due on January 4, 2027.
What We Found and How
The SSR draft rolls are machine readable. We took every voter whose entry names a father or a mother, and looked in the same booth for a voter with that name living in the same house. If that ‘parent’ turned out to be the same age as the voter, or younger, we flagged the entry.
We found 1,10,875 such cases spread across all 75 districts and 403 constituencies.
In 35,523 of these cases, parent and child are the same age. In the other 75,352, the parent is younger, and in 6,860 of them by 20 years or more.
Some of the cases are shown below for representation:
What did SIR Actually Achieve?
The SIR was designed to weed out exactly this kind of error. It had enumeration forms, BLO visits, software flags and hearings. A parent who is younger than their own child is perhaps the most basic inconsistency a voter list can have. This raises a larger question: if a process this elaborate left the most basic errors untouched, what did the SIR actually achieve?
Moreover, spotting these anomalous entries is no rocket science. Each one is a contradiction between two lines of the same booth’s roll, often on the same page: An 87-year-old whose father is 23, a 123-year-old woman whose mother is 45, two women who are each other’s mother. A simple check on the roll itself would have thrown them up. Either no such check was run, or nobody acted on what it found.
As of now, all 1,10,875 are in the draft, and the window for corrections closes on December 16.
The district-wise and constituency-wise count of such cases is given below. Kushinagar district has the most cases (3,646), and Fazilnagar has the most for a single assembly constituency (711).
Skip to PDF content
In a related report published on November 21, Alt News showed several glaring anomalies that the final SIR list for Uttar Pradesh had, including at least 230 voters listed multiple times across 69 booths, missing addresses, unexplained name and gender changes, and suspicious deletions. World Health Organization chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus called on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) for the immediate lifting of the U.S. fuel blockade on Cuba, ‌warning that the measure was putting the lives of children at risk.
“The intensification of fuel restrictions and sanctions is causing direct harm to the Cuban people, especially the most vulnerable,” Mr. Tedros said on ‌a recent visit to Cuba that included tours of several healthcare facilities in ‌Havana.
“It is endangering their lives, including the ‌lives of children.”
During his three-day visit, the official said his organization would contribute $2 million to help strengthen Cuba’s national immunization program and provide essential medical equipment to healthcare facilities.
Like the World Health Organization, ‌the United Nations has also repeatedly warned of a growing humanitarian crisis on the island, calling the U.S. fuel blockade a violation of international ‌law and the human rights of all Cubans.
The Cuban government says U.S. sanctions have led to daily power outages lasting 20 hours or more, critical shortages of medicines and surgical supplies, and a decline in health indicators, such ‌as infant mortality rates.
Washington argues the energy blockade is intended to push for political change on the island, and says that exports of food and medicine are subject to legal exemptions.
Tensions between the two nations have soared since the ‌administration of U.S. President Donald Trump ramped up pressure on Cuba since January, imposing a fuel blockade on the island and stiff sanctions against a swath of Cuban officials and state entities.
An annual non-binding resolution calling for an end to a U.S. embargo on the island ‌has passed in favor of Cuba in the UN General Assembly by wide margins every year since 1992.

The COVID-19 pandemic is having a devastating impact across the world. Efforts to contain the coronavirus are vital to the health of the world’s population, but they are also exposing children to increased risk of violence – including maltreatment, gender-based violence and sexual exploitation.
As leaders of organisations committed to ending violence against children, we come together in solidarity to share our deep concern, call for action and pledge our support to protect children from violence and reduce the impact of COVID-19 on children in every country and community.
A third of the global population is on COVID-19 lockdown, and school closures have impacted more than 1.5 billion children. Movement restrictions, loss of income, isolation, overcrowding and high levels of stress and anxiety are increasing the likelihood that children experience and observe physical, psychological and sexual abuse at home – particularly those children already living in violent or dysfunctional family situations. And while online communities have become central to maintain many children’s learning, support and play, it is also increasing their exposure to cyberbullying, risky online behavior and sexual exploitation.
The situation is aggravated by children’s lack of access to schoolfriends, teachers, social workers and the safe space and services that schools provide. The most vulnerable children – including refugees, migrants, and children who are internally displaced, deprived of liberty, living without parental care, living on the street and in urban slums, with disabilities, and living in conflict-affected areas – are a particular concern. For many, growing economic vulnerability will increase the threat of child labour, child marriage and child trafficking.
We must act now. Together, we call on governments, the international community and leaders in every sector to urgently respond with a united effort to protect children from the heightened risk of violence, exploitation and abuse as part of the broader response to COVID-19.
Governments have a central role to play. They must ensure that COVID-19 prevention and response plans integrate age appropriate and gender sensitive measures to protect all children from violence, neglect and abuse. Child protection services and workers must be designated as essential and resourced accordingly.
Working with and supporting governments, our collective response must include: maintaining essential health and social welfare services, including mental health and psychosocial support; providing child protection case management and emergency alternative care arrangements; ensuring social protection for the most vulnerable children and households; continuing care and protection for children in institutions; and communicating with and engaging parents, caregivers and children themselves with evidence-based information and advice. National helplines, school counsellors and other child-friendly reporting mechanisms enable children in distress to reach out for help, and must be adapted to the challenges of COVID-19.
Given the heightened risks of online harms, technology companies and telecoms providers must do everything they can to keep children safe online. This includes providing access to cost-free child helplines, age-appropriate services and safe e-education platforms - and using their platforms to share child online safety advice. They must also do more to detect and stop harmful activity against children online, including grooming and the creation and distribution of child sexual abuse images and videos.
As global organisations working to end violence against children, we will continue to advocate for and invest in effective child protection solutions. We will collectively develop and share technical resources and guidance for policymakers, practitioners, parents, caregivers and children themselves. And we will support the courageous health, child protection and humanitarian professionals working around the clock to keep children safe during these unprecedented times.
In recent years, the global community has made significant gains in protecting children from violence. We must not allow those gains to be lost during the current turmoil. We must do all we can to keep children safe now. And we must plan ahead together, so that once the immediate health crisis is over, we can get back on track towards the goal of ending all forms of violence, abuse and neglect of children

Virginia reported its first measles-associated death of 2026 on Friday, November 20, 2026, involving a child who tested positive for measles, the state health department said.
The department said the child was between 0 and 4 years old. It did not disclose additional details, including the child's vaccination status, citing the family's privacy.
Measles can cause serious complications, including pneumonia, brain inflammation, complications during pregnancy and death.
Virginia has reported 220 measles cases so far in 2026, including 40 among children aged 0 to 4 and 75 among those aged 5 to 12, state health department data showed as of November 19. Of those cases, 179 were in unvaccinated individuals, 39 were in people whose vaccination status was unknown and two were in vaccinated individuals.
Virginia health officials have reported increased measles activity driven largely by outbreaks in central region. Buckingham County has reported 127 cases, the highest in the state, while neighbouring Charlotte County has recorded 34 cases.
The death adds to a worsening national measles outbreak that this week cost the United States its measles elimination status after 26 years.
Pennsylvania, the hardest-hit U.S. state, reported an eighth measles-related death and confirmed 1,631 measles cases, as of November 20. Wisconsin has also reported two deaths, while New York state recorded its first measles-associated death, involving a child.
The CDC has confirmed six measles-associated deaths so far in 2026, though it does not specify the states where the deaths were recorded.
A discrepancy between state and federal death tallies arose earlier this year after the CDC, under US Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., began using National Center for Health Statistics mortality data instead of state figures.
The sharp increase in U.S. measles cases has coincided with declining immunization rates and rising vaccine hesitancy under Kennedy, who has for years spread doubts, without scientific evidence, about the safety of measles vaccines.

China investigates Politburo member and Shanghai party chief Chen Jining
BANGKOK — Chinese Communist Party authorities are investigating Shanghai party secretary Chen Jining for suspected violations of party discipline, China's anti-corruption watchdog said Tuesday.
The Politburo member is the latest senior official targeted in President Xi Jinping's long-running anti-corruption campaign, which has shown no signs of letting up in scope or depth.
Chen is under investigation by the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection. The brief announcement by China's Central Commission for Discipline Inspection provided no further details.
A statement released by the Shanghai city government said the Standing Committee of the Shanghai Committee of the CCP "expressed firm support" for the decision to investigate Chen.
The decision sent "a clear and powerful signal that the fight against corruption would continue without pause or retreat," but with "a firm determination to win," the statement said.
The investigation follows sweeping purges under Xi, who has emphasized greater party discipline. The Chinese leader has pursued an anti-corruption campaign for more than a decade, carrying out purges on a scale not seen since Mao Zedong's rule.
"The takedown again shows that Xi Jinping's anti-corruption campaign has no limits," Mingda Qiu, a senior analyst at Eurasia Group, said in an emailed statement. "This is the fourth Politburo member to fall, and the fourth sitting member brought down in the current cycle. The pattern is unprecedented."
The recent Politburo purges highlight how much Chinese politics depend on shifting circumstances, with even officials with qualities that Xi apparently valued being vulnerable to removal, said Joseph Torigian, a professor at American University based in Washington.
"On paper," they appear to be "individuals Xi would appreciate," Torigian said, but afterward, "we could easily come up with hypotheses for why he got rid of them."
Other Politburo members purged include Gen. Zhang Youxia and He Weidong, both senior members of the Central Military Commission, which oversees the armed forces, and Ma Xingrui, a provincial party secretary.
The post of Shanghai party secretary has traditionally been viewed as a stepping stone to China's top leadership. The country's former President Jiang Zemin, its current premier, Li Qiang, and Xi himself previously held the position.
Chen has served as Shanghai party secretary since 2022. He previously held senior positions in Beijing's municipal government and headed the Ministry of Environmental Protection.

The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) said it had cancelled the drug manufacturing licences of Pune-based Inducare Pharmaceutical and Research Foundation for the second time after the firm was found to have manufactured and sold nine drugs without mandatory product permission, all of which were subsequently declared substandard, misbranded or spurious by government analysts.
The cancellation order, issued on November 23 by the Joint Commissioner (Drugs), Pune Division, directed the firm to immediately cease all manufacturing, packing, testing and distribution activities. The FDA has also proposed prosecution against the firm under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940.
Of the nine drugs tested, two were declared spurious after government analysts found that the claimed active ingredients were absent. Ibucare Plus, a combination of ibuprofen and paracetamol, contained no ibuprofen, while Carevita-M, a multivitamin tablet, was found to contain none of the nine specified ingredients tested.
The remaining drugs failed various quality tests, with several containing significantly lower quantities of active ingredients than claimed on their labels. These included medicines used in the treatment of cardiovascular and digestive disorders.
The FDA said the firm, located in the Additional MIDC area of Jejuri in Pune district, had admitted in its written response that it had not obtained separate product permissions for the nine drugs.
Earlier violations
The firm’s manufacturing licences had previously been cancelled on September 7 after a joint inspection conducted on July 14 and 15 revealed 25 serious deficiencies in Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP).
The inspection revealed that approximately 13.86 lakh tablets of Caregyl-400 had been manufactured without mandatory batch manufacturing and packing records or test reports. Of these, 5.20 lakh tablets had already been distributed. Laboratory analysis revealed that the sampled batch contained only 32.44% of the claimed metronidazole content.
Several samples of substandard drugs were also collected from the Central Medical Store of Yashwantrao Chavan Memorial (YCM) Hospital in Pimpri-Chinchwad, following which stocks worth approximately ₹1.72 crore were seized on November 4.
Other irregularities included discrepancies in manufacturing and expiry dates, inadequate laboratory testing procedures, unhygienic manufacturing conditions and improper storage of finished products.
Risk to patients
A show-cause notice was issued to the firm on October 29, following which it submitted a written response on November 3. A personal hearing was conducted on November 23.
The licensing authority rejected the firm’s contention that no patient complaints had been received, observing that the risk of treatment failure arising from spurious and substandard drugs existed even in the absence of complaints.
“Ensuring that citizens have access to safe, quality and efficacious drugs is the foremost responsibility of the Food and Drug Administration. Stringent regulatory and legal action will be taken against any manufacturer who plays with the health of the general public by manufacturing drugs without product permission,” FDA Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe said.

State AGs are trying to stop Character.AI from auctioning off users' chat histories
The proposed sale would include explicit conversations with children, officials say.
Character.AI is still drawing controversy and legal scrutiny even during its bankruptcy proceedings. A group of 42 attorneys general are trying to block the chatbot company from auctioning off users' chat histories and other sensitive information.
The company, which had faced numerous investigations and lawsuits over its safety record, filed for bankruptcy last month. The company said at the time that it would begin a "a court-supervised sale of all or substantially all of our assets" but that users data would continue to be "protected" by its privacy policy.
But the auction for Character.AI won't actually safeguard users' data at all, according to the state AGs. "Character.AI's plan to auction off its platform, including the IP addresses and private chats histories of its users — many of them children — with zero protection for those users is appalling," California Attorney General Rob Bonta said in a statement. "If this sale goes through, users' sensitive data would go into the hands of a buyer even though Character.AI promised consumers that their data would not be sold."
According to Bonta's office, the proposed sale includes chat histories, including conversations "in which AI characters drew children and adults into explicit sexual conversations." The buyer would also get access to chats in which users interacted with AI characters posing as physicians and therapists and discussed self harm, eating disorders, suicidal thoughts and other sensitive topics.
The AGs have also raised concerns about the fact that only one anonymous bidder has been disclosed so far. That entity, called Smirks and Pangs Acquisition LLC, was formed "one day before Character.AI picked it as the base bid for the auction," and its source of funding hasn't been disclosed. "Nothing in the agreement restricts what the buyer may do with the data after closing, including selling it," the AGs say in a court filing.
The auction is currently scheduled for December 1. The AGs are asking the bankruptcy court to block the sale to Smirks and deny a "break-up fee" that would allow the company to collect $350,000 if Character.AI sells to another buyer. They're also asking for children's chatbot conversations and "sensitive" data to be barred from any potential sale.
"Children and families who shared their most personal thoughts with Character.AI never imagined those conversations could be auctioned off to the highest bidder," Colorado Attorney General Phil Weiser said in a statement. "A company's financial troubles do not give it the right to disregard its responsibility to protect consumers, especially children.

It wasn’t until I was stuck in traffic on the way back from a run up and down some canyon roads that I realized just how low Porsche’s upcoming all-electric 718 Boxster truly is. I was idly looking around at the other cars, doing the math on the EV adoption rate in this small sample of Los Angeles gridlock (roughly 50 percent, impressively) when I noticed that I was eye-level with a Tesla Model Y door handle.
That’s not particularly low for a sports car, but it’s practically unheard of for an EV. Nearly all modern electric cars are built atop a skateboard-style battery pack, a stack of cells that elevates the seating position by a good 3 inches. In these SUV-heady days, that’s usually not a problem, possibly even an advantage. But, in a car like this, the closer you can get your keister to the road, the greater the sensation of speed.
So, for the company’s first all-electric sports car, the 718 Boxster that will be fully revealed next year, Porsche engineers put the battery pack behind the driver. That powers a single motor spinning the rear wheels and creates a driving experience that both honors the simple joy of motoring in a mid-engined Boxster while pushing the 718 to new heights of power and performance.
Mid-engined? Mid-batteried.
That EV battery layout, stacked behind the two-seat cabin rather than sandwiched below it, isn’t novel. It’s the same setup that Tesla used on the original Roadster back in 2008. Back then it was done for cost reasons as much as anything, enabling Tesla to repurpose a Lotus chassis meant to hold an internal combustion engine in the middle.
For Porsche’s new Boxster (and the Audi Concept C, which is built on the same platform), that pack enables the low seating position and also delivers a rearward weight bias (40:60 front/rear) that’s in keeping with the last-generation 718 Boxster, the internal combustion model killed by EU cybersecurity regulations last year.

The Best Espresso Machines for Home Baristas
Featured in this article
The Best espresso machines for home must thread a delicate needle. Espresso is forceful and finicky, and a little intimidating, and yet so essential that astronauts might take it into orbit. A home espresso machine remains the most intense and expensive device I regularly operate before my first cup of coffee.
I tend to favor devices that let technology do much of the work and don't make you join a cult of engineers before your first cup. And so my top-rated espresso machine, the Fellow Series 1, earned its place on WIRED's counter by combining ease of use with a solid build, consistent temperature, and rare control over pressure—an industry-beating mix of nerdiness and hand-holding friendliness. For a more classic, all-analog build, we offer the compact, stylish Diletta Mio.
But I also know not everyone wants to also buy a good coffee grinder or spend four figures for their morning cup. For those who want milk-based drinks and a built-in grinder, I recommend the top-selling Breville Barista Express as the Goldilocks machine balancing performance and cost. For an entry-level device, I pretty much always recommend the straight-ahead Breville Bambino, among the lowest-cost machines with PID-controlled temperature.
Note that this guide mostly covers classic, hands-on espresso machines with portafilters. We do also include the De'Longhi Rivelia, our top pick among super-automatic espresso machines that require little more than a button press. For a guide that focuses on easy-to-use espresso machine picks that do most of the work for you, check out our guide to the Best Latte and Automatic Espresso Machines.

Frequently Asked Questions
How Do I Test Espresso Machines?
Over the past decade, WIRED has tested dozens of espresso makers to find our favorites. The process, in part, is simple. We brew a whole lot of coffee. I’ve written about coffee for more than a decade on both the East and West Coasts, including my hometown coffee mecca of Portland, Oregon. Other current and past WIRED espresso testers—who include former baristas and longtime coffee writers—include Jaina Grey, Jeffrey Van Camp, Kat Merck, Tyler Shane, Pete Cottell, and Scott Gilbertson.
On each machine that’s capable, I make and assess at least four styles of drink, on multiple roasts and beans: a basic 2:1 espresso, an Americano, a latte, and a cappuccino. On machines that advertise a wacky array of drinks, I test each one. This includes any newfangled coldspresso and head-scratching variations on a “long.” It also includes, if science dictates, espresso martinis. And I test to see whether a machine can be dialed to both dark roasts and lighter roasts.
I might make many dozens of coffees to dial in a machine and truly understand it, and on any of my top picks I've made at least fifty drinks. Sometimes, alas, you understand a machine’s shortcomings far sooner—and so some of our less-recommended devices are dismissed a bit earlier.
What I’m looking for is nuance, aromatics, beauty, sensitivity to the characteristics of each bean, and the satisfying texture of fully integrated milk. But also, I’m looking for ease, the thoughtful touches that make an espresso maker something you can fall in love with.
I test whether the hot water spout splatters, whether descaling requires a degree in hydrology, whether the brewing temperature is consistent, and whether the latte milk gets silked. I’m truly terrible at latte art, but whether it’s possible is a straightforward test of the body of the frothed milk. I test the airier foam of cappuccinos and compare manual and automatic milk frothing on machines that try to froth milk for you. I test how fast the wand steams and whether it’s easy to fully integrate milk before the dang thing starts to burn your milk.
On machines with built-in grinders, I both assess the grind and weigh the dose—and then weigh it again. And then again. Consistency is the hobgoblin of little cups. I also test multiple grind settings to make sure the grind is consistent.
On any semiautomatic machine that decides the shot size for you, I test this to see whether you're getting a ristretto or a lungo by default. Then I resolve never to say the word “lungo” again.
I don’t generally take apart the machines I’m sent, but I do quite often look up videos of people who do—and look at how the thing’s constructed under the hood.
How I Select Espresso Machines to Review
In part, we select machines to test by looking at the espresso makers with long track records of making good espresso machines—people with long tails in the industry and good track records of customer support. Names like Breville, De'Longhi, La Marzocco, and Rancilio. But also, I listen. I read. I ask every coffee-obsessive in my life. I pay attention to the newest releases, follow trade shows, watch Youtube videos, and spend a lot of time tracking down not just the obious big names but the unexpected recommendations.
I often also look at how accessible each machine will be to most users. Espresso isn’t just a finicky process: It’s finicky by design. The most sensitive and sophisticated traditional machines are responsive to every tiny variation in the coffee grind and every fluctuation in the water temperature. The deepest bean geeks want this: They want the control, the frustration, the vision quest.
But I also know that most of you out there aren’t looking to be in an abusive relationship with your coffee machine. Few want to wake up to feelings of inadequacy, brought on by a machine that costs as much as a used car. And so what I look for is the espresso machines that can pull lovely character from each bean, but also make this easy on you.
This means that our top picks, the ones I recommend to most people, tend to fall in the semiautomatic camp: They’re the ones that offer the best coffee with the least effort. Finding this balance is delicate and often rewarding. It used to be that a built-in grinder was a recipe for blown shots, sadness, or pressurized portafilters with less character. But year by year, espresso machine makers get better at this goal.
The lowest-cost machines I recommend tend to offer more forgiving pressurized filter baskets as options, even though these sacrifice a bit of nuance for forgiveness, because I don’t want to assume you’re pairing a $200 espresso machine with a $2,000 coffee grinder. Although I know some of you do this, especially with our beloved Breville Bambino.
But hey, if you’re a tinkerer for life, and want to join modding groups? We recommend a machine for you, too. Mostly so you can disagree on Reddit, and explain why your favorite is better.
What Beans Are Best for Espresso?
First off, there's no such thing as “espresso beans,” whatever it says on the bag you buy. Espresso beans are coffee beans, ground finely enough to be pressed into service as espresso.
But traditionally, espresso is made with darker-roast beans that best elicit the deep, chocolatey notes of classic Italian espresso. In fact, most machines you use are probably designed with dark-roast beans in mind: Darker beans grind easier, extract easier, and are a bit more homogeneous across the market. And so when someone writes “espresso roast” or “espresso blend” on their grind, that's often what they mean.
Does that mean dark roast is the only espresso? Of course not. Modern craft and premium coffee roasters in the United States have begun trending toward medium and medium-dark roasts that offer a bit more balance, character, and even a little acidity—beans that have more aromatics, and more individuality. Some, including me, love experimenting with truly light roasts, including the lightest of natural-processed beans that let me brew up espresso that tastes like strawberries.
It's up to you. But note that the lighter the roast, the more you'll need to adjust grind and temperature to accommodate—and sometimes even go off-script entirely. (See here for an explainer on light-roast espresso.) But the classic recommendations for espresso? Pulling a 25- to 30-second shot, at a steady 9 bars of pressure, at a 2:1 ratio for a standard shot? These were all designed for traditional dark-roast beans.
One thing that's true, however, is that you should use fresh beans. They'll taste better and more aromatic, sure. But stale beans exposed to oxygen also make it technically difficult to make good espresso: they've begun to break down, often allow channeling, and are more likely to lead to a less evenly extracted shot with funny off-flavors.
Obviously, fresh beans are easiest to obtain from a local roaster, and on the plus side you'll be able to ask the baristas there how best to make espresso from their beans. But when in doubt in a supermarket, look for a roast date on the bag. If you can't find it, or if your beans were roasted in Italy and sent on a ship? Chances are they're not fresh. And your espresso will be worse. For fresh beans delivered to your house, check out WIRED's guide to the best coffee subscriptions.
Espresso Accessories That Make for Great Cups
If you're spending this much on an espresso machine, you'll want to invest in a good grinder and even a scale, as well as a few other devices that make your shots better, and your life a little easier.
An espresso-capable grinder: If your espresso machine doesn't come with a grinder, you'll need one. Preground bag beans are especially difficult to use when making espresso, and will likely lead to off-flavors or channeling. But not just any grinder will do. You'll need a good grinder that can grind consistent beans finely enough for espresso. WIRED's top-pick Baratza Encore ESP is always a good choice—positioned squarely at the fulcrum where more expensive grinders begin to offer diminishing returns.
An accurate scale with a timer: Most grinders, and a goodly portion of espresso machines, do not offer a precise scale. But a precise scale is what you need to get espresso ratios right. WIRED reviewer Julian Chokkattu loved the Acaia brew-by-weight scale ($400) that automatically connects to the La Marzocco Linea Mini and a few other devices via its companion app. But a far less sophisticated scale can still help you measure your shot size and control the dose you want on each espresso shot. If you're not precious about beauty, there's always this low-cost, little no-name scale. It's accurate to a 10th of a gram, and has a timer to boot.
The best knockbox: When you're done with that portafilter filled with coffee grounds, what do you do with it? Beat it against the side of a trashcan? Dig out those grounds into the sink? Nah. You need a good knock box. And somehow this jobby-job from Breville is the best one I've ever found. It's sturdy, the cross bar is in the right spot so that the grinds dump cleanly into the bin, and the bottom has enough grip that the box doesn't scoot around on the counter. Simplicity is competence.
Not all steaming pitchers are created equal, notes WIRED contributing reviewer (and former barista) Pete Cottell. As opposed to the sad piece of aluminum that probably came with your espresso maker, this Brewista offers thick walls for heat retention, a precision tip for expert latte pours, and a thermometer sticker on its side so you can get a rough gauge of milk temperature without hunting down an actual thermometer. It can also take a beating. This is your new frothing pitcher.
Other Machines We Like
Breville Oracle Jet for $2,000: The Breville Oracle Jet is my previous top pick for threading that delicate needle between ease and deliciousness, before getting displaced by my new top-pick Fellow device. The Oracle Jet remains a powerful and frankly beautiful stainless-steel machine, with sterling temperature control and a solid built-in grinder that uses the same conical burrs as the excellent Baratza Encore ESP ($200). This Oracle Jet will pull beautiful nuances from beans ranging from berry-light to chocolate dark, on drinks ranging from an Americano to a flat white to “cold espresso” best placed in a martini. And yet the Jet's easily accessible for anyone who can figure out an iPhone, with a touchscreen tutorial, digital guidance on finding the right grind for each bean, and automatic tamping and steaming. You'll be nose-deep in a cappuccino within 20 minutes of pulling this thing out of the box. Note that manual milk steaming with the Jet's powerful wand is still better than the automatic version.
Ninja Luxe Cafe Pro for $750: Tradition is the opposite of what Ninja does. This is the company that made the soft-serve Swirl, the Slushi, and the portable air fryer. Ninja is all about the extras. And Ninja doesn't judge. And so of course Ninja jumped in with both feet on cold-foam coldspresso. In fact, the new Luxe Cafe Pro makes the best cold foam out of any espresso machine I've tried, with a whisk that whips up plant milk or cow milk into thick, creamy, dense, beautiful froth—ready for your ridiculously complicated cold caramel-vanilla latte TikTok recipe. What I didn't expect was that Ninja would also nail the fundamentals so well, on only its second entry into the espresso market. The relatively accurate by-weight dosing is nice. So is the excellent steam wand that also outpaces most contenders on automatic hot foaming, adjustable to multiple densities of foam. The Pro clears up some oversights in the previous-model Premier, including an easy tamping lever, and a hot water spout. Maintenance, whether descaling or purging, is also as easy as it gets. Just don't use this grinder with light roast beans. Medium or dark only.
Breville Oracle Dual Boiler for $3,000: This update to the previous Breville Dual Boiler espresso machine is a powerful, truly impressive machine in many regards. It combines the easy touchscreen operation and automatic dosing and tamping of WIRED's previous top-pick Oracle Jet with a welcome “manual” mode that lets you play with pre-infusion and bloom while monitoring a digital pressure gauge on the touchscreen. I kinda love this as an exercise in future-retro design—or whatever the inverse of steampunk is—but also as a means of really controlling my shot, and getting a lot more crema and body out of it. The dual boiler heats up very fast—like four minutes fast—and gives you the wonderful temperature stability and consistency you expect from a dual boiler, plus the ability to steam milk and make espresso simultaneously. The production model I received had a very tight portafilter fit, which loosened up after the first 30 shots or so but initially required some muscle. I also haven't been able to get good results with lighter-roast beans, which led to the occasional under-filled portafilter that had to be retamped manually. We'll update as we resolve those quirks, but can attest that for medium to dark beans, this Dual Boiler is an absolute beast.
Meraki Espresso Machine for $1,999: Meraki is a young Hong Kong–based company. Last year, it was still Kickstarting funds for its debut Meraki Espresso Machine. But the company started off with a bang, with a premium semiautomatic double-boiler machine offering features you don't find even in machines that cost hundreds more. This means a Timemore grinder that'll grind by weight within two-tenths of a gram precision. PID temperature control. Easy pre-infusion. A quiet rotary pump. Another scale under the brewer that lets you control output. A powerful steam wand that regulates the temperature of froth within about 3 degrees for whatever milk drinks strike your fancy. A tamper with satisfying heft, and a tamping station that feels like luxury. Frankly, despite having to overrotate the portafilter for proper fit, its wondrous aesthetics and ease made it a contender for our top picks. But service is always a worry among newer, direct-to-consumer entrants, and the wackily complicated descaling procedure makes maintenance a concern.
Ninja Luxe Cafe Premier for $600: Ninja has already released an upgraded Ninja Luxe Cafe Pro version ($750) after its espresso machine debut. But its first device, the Luxe Cafe Premier, is already a corker, a low-priced all-in-one with cold brew, coffee, espresso, excellent milk frothing, and unexpected luxury features like a built-in scale so the grinder can dose by weight. The device can feel either overstuffed or generous, depending on who you are. Either way this damn near unseated the Breville Barista Express as WIRED's mid-tier top pick, aside from a few leaks and sensible caution about its durability.
De'Longhi La Specialista Opera for $900: Speaking of espresso makers that came running at Breville, this Opera is a beautifully forgiving semiautomatic machine that makes excellent espresso in the medium- to dark-roast range, with non-pressurized portafilter baskets that make for a nice and surprisingly subtle cup. It's the best De'Longhi espresso machine I've tested, in many ways, among the semiautomatic camp. The Opera sports a lot of options—including dose and temperature control—while remaining refreshingly analog with its satisfying metal frame, metal buttons, and prominent pressure gauge. Cold brew is a perk for those who like milk. The grinder is decent, though its 15 settings might not offer enough sensitivity to pull the best from each roast. One could wish for a removable hopper and a sturdier tamping lever. But if you or your partner love cold coffee drinks or espresso martinis, this gives comparable Brevilles a strong run for the money.
De'Longhi La Specialista Touch for $1,000: De'Longhi's new Touch, released this year, isn't merely a touchscreen version of the very analog Opera—though it is just as handsome as the Opera. Instead, it offers a very specific set of trade-offs. Like De'Longhi's Rivelia, there's a bean-assist function that you can save for each bean you like. It's also got a better steam wand, with the ability to read the temperature of the milk you're steaming, as you steam it. In fact, it's maybe more intuitive overall. But it doesn't quite offer the easy customization on temperature, shot time, or ratios. The cold brew is not quite as well-dialed as the Opera. The Touch is an Italian machine on training wheels, designed for Italian-style medium to dark shots. This should work for most people, but minus a pressure bar or a shot timer, it can also feel like a bit of a black box.
La Marzocco Linea Mini for $6,600: WIRED reviewer Julian Chokkattu spent two weeks with La Marzocco's Linea Mini, a home version of the fancy espresso machines you'll see in coffee shops around the world. The price may be eye-searing, but Chokkattu did find the resulting elixir to be absolutely fantastic—and the same went for La Marzocco's customer service while Chokkattu was dialing in his machine. It offers a lot of room for experimentation, and sports a killer cool-touch steam wand that froths milk in seconds.
De'Longhi Stilosa for $150: The Stilosa was our top budget pick for years. It's still a good budget pick, and it often goes on sale for less than $100. You're not going to get high-end features like a pressure gauge or built-in grinder, and it's a little plasticky. But what the Stilosa does provide is everything you need to make great espresso at home: a solid portafilter, a reliable steam pump, and a steaming wand. It is a little light, so you'll want to brace it when you mount and dismount the portafilter (or it might slide around on you). After brewing cup after cup of espresso, the Stilosa never showed signs of slowing or breaking down the way many inexpensive machines can. In fact, we're now revisiting the Stilosa as our budget pick, after catching a few tips on how to use the Stilosa for light roast espresso.
Breville Barista Express Impress for $800: This espresso machine is the more tricked-out sibling of the Breville Barista Express. It includes more grind and dosing settings and automates some of the more complicated parts of brewing consistently good espresso, like getting just the right amount of beans ground per shot.
Breville Dual Boiler for $1,600: The previous-generation Breville Dual Boiler is an absolute tank of an espresso machine. It's huge. It's heavy. It makes amazing espresso. But while its size makes brewing espresso feel luxurious, it does eat up a lot of space and needs a little time to heat up, versus newer Brevilles like the Oracle Jet that favor thermoblock-style heaters. But a dual boiler does mean you can brew shot after shot, with steamed milk and hot water at the same time, without having to wait in between shots. The new Breville Oracle Dual Boiler ($3,000) is already on the market, but you can still pick up the previous generation for half the price.
Cuisinart EM-160 Slim for $250: The lowest-cost espresso maker from Cuisinart's new espresso line is among the slimmer espresso machines out there, less than 7 inches across. This makes it a treasure for certain kitchens. The espresso quality is about what you'd expect from a pressurized portafilter: smoother, less nuanced, but also pretty forgiving for beginners trying to dial in a bean. This'll be best for those who mix milk with their espresso. Same goes for the fast-dripped “cold espresso” option, which takes a couple minutes to complete and comes out a bit tannic, but mixes well with cold milk or a lot of ice. You'll need a grinder if you don't want sad supermarket beans.
Superkop Manual Espresso Maker for $600: This manual espresso machine is technically not a Jackie Chan movie. The Superkop is instead a quite finely engineered espresso device. It looks pretty, and unlike other manual espresso machines, you don't need a strong arm to use it. So if you want to pull espresso, but not pull it hard, the Superkop is your huckleberry. That said, $600 is a lot of money for a manual device. Buy it if you know you'll love it.
Also Tried
Gevi Espresso Machine With Grinder and Milk Frother for $350: WIRED contributing reviewer Pete Cottell prized the pressure control and built-in grinder on this Gevi espresso machine, when you take into account the near-unfathomable low price for a machine with this functionality. Alas, a somewhat erratic steam wand makes it hard to recommend.
Cuisinart EM-640 Espresso Bar for $650: Cuisinart rolled in with some ambition on this semiautomatic espresso machine, with a built-in grinder and a non-pressurized, bottomless portafilter meant to play in the same sandbox as Breville's top devices. Alas, I really couldn't get consistency on either dosing or grinding from the device's built-in grinder—and the system for customizing the dose in particular was mostly wild guesswork. This all added up to botched shots, wild spray from the portafilter, and none of the ease one wants from a semiautomatic.
De'Longhi La Specialista Arte Evo for $675: This semiautomatic De'Longhi La Specialista Arte Evo comes with a built-in burr grinder makes great espresso right out of the box, and is slimmer than other espresso machines in its category, It does have quirks: It includes a little plastic adapter needed to attach the portafilter to the grinder spout, and a little stepstool for your espresso cup to keep the coffee from splashing. It's a good machine, but I'd upgrade to the Opera any day of the week.

There will be a new president at the helm of a new-look Indian Olympic Association, but who it might be remains unclear.
Incumbent P.T. Usha did not turn up on the final day of filing nominations for the upcoming Executive Council elections, effectively marking the end of her innings as the first woman IOA president, even as Tuesday saw more activity at the IOA Bhawan here than in a long time.
While former Secretary General and Fencing Association of India secretary Rajeev Mehta set the ball rolling with his nomination for the top spot on Monday, the final hours saw most of the prospective contestants rolling in to file their nominations. Current vice-president and Olympic medalist shooter Gagan Narang has emerged as a frontrunner, but Archery Association of India’s secretary and Delhi BJP leader Virender Sachdeva is also in the fray, making it a three-way contest.
Sachdeva, however, has also filed for the male vice-president’s spot, along with boxer Vijender Singh, while Anju Bobby George is being challenged by Bhavneet Handoo of wushu and Suman Kaushik from netball for the female VP post. Former table tennis player Kamlesh Mehta is set to be the next treasurer as the lone candidate.
Senior VP Ajay Patel is seeking another term, with Mona Shah (swimming) and netball’s Vagish Pathak challenging him. Sunaina Kumari and Amitabh Sharma are among those fighting to be joint secretaries, along with archer Purnima Mahato and ice hockey’s Harjinder Singh. The nominations also present interesting permutations with Vijender and Harjinder being proposed by Usha.
With some of the big names from the present EC missing out, including treasurer and weightlifting boss Sahdev Yadav, football chief Kalyan Choubey – who, incidentally, is the proposer for Narang -- and shuttler Saina Nehwal, one of the four elected Sportsperson of Outstanding Merit (SOM), the next leadership of the IOA is expected to have a new look, leading India’s sporting organisation for the next four years.
Rani Rampal and Yogeshwar Dutt have filed for the SOM quota of EC and are set to be nominated unopposed, while Dola Banerjee, Bhupinder Singh Bajwa, R.N. Jayaprakash, Prashant Kushwaha, Vitthal Shirgaonkar, Mona and Suman Kaushik are in the fray for the remaining four EC spots.
Elections are scheduled for December 5 for 13 positions – President, senior vice-president and treasurer (one each), vice-presidents and joint secretaries (two each, one male and one female) and six EC members including two from among the Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit (SOM) elected earlier.
However, with the sports ministry and political circles keen on unanimous choices and the last date of withdrawal of names being December 2 till 5 pm, the next week is set to see more action in the corridors of sporting power than on the field. It also remains to be seen if Usha presents India’s bid to the IOC’s Future Hosts Commission for the 2036 Olympics, scheduled for Thursday.

Andy Taylor, the original guitarist of the 1980s English new wave band Duran Duran, has died aged 65.
Taylor's death was confirmed by his family and bandmates in a statement posted on social media and Duran Duran's website.
He died after a "long and courageous battle with prostate cancer", the statement said.
"From the moment he arrived in Birmingham from the North East with a guitar and an unshakeable belief in what we could become, he brought an indelible fire and swagger to our music," the band said.
"His playing drove the songs that took us around the world, and with a dry wit that was matched only by his wonderfully unsentimental, no-nonsense outlook on life he kept us grounded and gave the band its edge through the extraordinary years that followed."
On the night he was inducted in the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in 2022, Taylor revealed that he had been battling stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer for several years and was unable to attend.
"I would like to thank each of my brothers in this great band," he wrote.
"You can dream about what happened to us but to experience it, on one's own terms, as mates, was beyond incredible."
The band's pop hits include Hungry Like the Wolf, The Reflex and Rio. The rise up the charts of Hungry Like a Wolf was inextricably linked to the launch of MTV.
The two-time Grammy Award-winners had nine gold and six platinum records, with 20 top-20 singles in the UK and 18 in the US.
The two-time Ivor Novello Award winners are also MTV Video Visionary Award recipients.
The band's imperial stage came through a trio of hit albums between 1981 and 1983 that delivered dance-floor anthems as Girls on Film and Union of the Snake, and the moody ballads The Chauffeur and Save a Prayer.
Their cemented their popularity when they recorded the James Bond theme song A View to a Kill and earned a slot at Live Aid in 1985.
Mixing fashion, pioneering synthesisers and glam-pop swagger, the telegenic band were all over radio and young people's walls, with bassist John Taylor and singer Simon Le Bon becoming heart-throbs and the band being labelled part of the New Romantics.
Princess Diana was known to be a fan, and that meant a lot to the band.
"It worked well for us," drummer Roger Taylor told Rolling Stone.
"It was genuine. I don't think it was some sort of PR stunt. It was massive for us because she was the number one icon of the early 80s."
Success in the MTV era
The band's success was in large part to their videos, including their Antigua-set song Rio, which featured shots of the band in pastel suits sailing confidently on a yacht.
For the album Rio, they shot three music videos in Sri Lanka and two in Antigua, feeding MTV's need to have a stream of visuals, something classic rock did not have.

"A lot of the success of the album is down to the power of the videos and the way it made the band omnipresent around the globe," Le Bon told The Daily Beats in 2012.
Andy Taylor agreed: "I don't think we could have done it without MTV."
New wave's 'Fab Five'
John Taylor and keyboardist Nick Rhodes started the band as teenagers in the northern city of Birmingham in 1978.
The group's name was inspired by a character in the Jane Fonda-starring sci-fi movie Barbarella.
Roger Taylor, Le Bon and Andy Taylor joined soon after, with the British press referring to them as the Fab Five.
Andy Taylor answered an ad in Melody Maker music magazine for a live-wire guitarist. (None of the Taylors were related.)
"We all grew up on the same vinyl records and live gigs, from David Bowie to Roxy Music, The Sex Pistols and, of course, Chic," Andy Taylor wrote in a letter read by the band during their Rock Hall induction.
"I could go to all those places as a player and developed a hybrid guitar style that fitted this amazing concept of a band."
